Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:10:1.english: No, in sixty - And for each one [of the Sages, it is appraised] according to his view.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:12:1.hebrew: אין שמין קב בששים קבים - אם אכלה קב, אין שמים בששים קבים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:12:1.english: We do not appraise a kav relative to sixty kav - If [the animal] ate a kav, we do not appraise [it] relative to sixty kav.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:12:2.hebrew: מפני שמשביח מזיק - דששים קבים אין להם מכר, מפני שמרובין הן לעני ומועטין לבינוני וכל שכן לעשיר. ועוד, שאין קרחת קב ניכרת בששים קבים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:12:2.english: Because [it] benefits the damager - For sixty kav [of land] have no [ready] market, because they are too large for a poor person, too small for a person of average means, and all the more so for a wealthy person. And furthermore, because the bare patch of a kav is not noticeable in sixty kav.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:12:3.hebrew: ולא כור בששים כורין - אכלה כור תבואה, אין שמין אותה בששים כורין. מפני שפוגם מזיק. לפי שאדם המשופע בנכסים ותאב לקנות קרקע גדולה, קונה אותה כשהוא מוצאה בהרבה יותר מדמיו; ועוד, קרחת כור גדולה היא מאד. אלא כל סאה שמין בששים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:12:3.english: And not a kor relative to sixty kor - [If an animal] ate a kor of grain, we do not appraise it relative to sixty kor. Because [this] weakens [the position of] the damager: for a person who is abundant in property and eager to buy a large [tract of] land buys it, when he finds it, for much more than its value; and furthermore, a bare patch of a kor is very large. Rather, every se'ah is appraised relative to sixty [se'ah].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:13:1.english: "And not a kor" it should have [said] - Just as it teaches, "They do not appraise a kav," and does not teach, "a beit kav."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:14:1.english: A kav in a beit kor - Its bare patch is not visible.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:15:2.hebrew: אמר ליה - ריש גלותא, אני ראיתי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:15:2.english: He said to him - [The] Exilarch [said to him]: I saw [it].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:15:3.english: And three date palms were in a cluster - Three date palms, one next to the other.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:15:4.english: Persian law - Which is not Torah law.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:16:1.hebrew: אם אמרו - בס' להקל על המזיק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:16:1.english: If [the Sages] said - [that it is appraised] in sixty [times the area] to be lenient on the damager.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:16:2.english: Regarding damage [caused by] his property - [Referring to] that which his animal ate and caused damage.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:16:3.hebrew: יאמרו בנזקי גופו - שמזיק בעצמו בידים, שקצץ לדקל:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:16:3.english: Would they say [so] regarding damage [caused by] his body - That he causes damage himself directly, in that he cut down the date palm.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:17:1.english: One who destroys his vineyard - [Meaning] he ruined and destroyed [it].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:18:1.english: We read: "[It] broke off a sapling" - [Meaning] an animal that broke off a sapling.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:18:2.hebrew: גוזרי גזירות - קונסי קנסות, אדמון וחנן בן אבשלום, בפרק בתרא דכתובות:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:18:2.english: Those who issue decrees - Imposers of fines, [namely] Admon and Chanan ben Avishalom, [as mentioned] in the last chapter of Ketubot.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:18:3.english: Unripe blades of grain [chaziz] - Green fodder.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:18:4.hebrew: במשוייר שבה - רואין את הנותר לפי מה שתעלה כל ערוגה וערוגה בימי הקציר, ומשלם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:18:4.english: According to what remains of it - They assess what remains according to what each and every bed [of grain] will yield at harvest time, and he pays.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:18:5.english: How much it was worth - [How much] the land [was worth] to be sold when it was with the unripe grain.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:1:1.english: And to take care of it - To be careful and cautious with it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:8:1.english: How do we appraise - the beit se'ah of the Mishnah.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:8:2.hebrew: סאה בס' סאין - האי בית סאה דקתני במתני' דבשביל ערוגה אחת שמין בית סאה, לאו בית סאה באנפי נפשה שיימינן, דמכחישין ליה למזיק — לפי שבית סאה נמכרת ביוקר, לפי שמועט הוא ואינו מצוי לימכר, ועני שאין ידו משגת לדמי קרקע גדולה קונה אותו ביותר מדמיו, וקרחת ערוגה של קב או קביים חשיב לו לפי דמיו — אלא שמין ששים סאים כמה שוין, ורואין כמה דמים מגיעין לבית סאה, וחוזרין ושמין כמה נפחתו דמיו בשביל קרחת ערוגה זו. וא"ת: למה הוזכר בית סאה? שאם היה שמין מתחלה הערוגה בששים סאין, כמה היו יפין וכמה הן יפין, לא היה משלם כלום, שאין קרחת ערוגה קטנה ניכרת בששים סאין, אבל בבית סאה ניכרת:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:8:2.english: A se'ah relative to sixty se'ah - This beit se'ah that the Mishnah teaches — that on account of one garden-bed we appraise a beit se'ah — we do not appraise a beit se'ah by itself, for [by doing so] we would be disadvantaging the damager — because a beit se'ah is sold dearly, since it is small and is not commonly available for sale, and a poor person whose means do not reach the price of a large tract of land buys it for more than its [true] value, and [thus] the bare patch of a garden-bed of a kav or two kavs is reckoned for him according to its [inflated] price — rather, we appraise how much sixty se'ah are worth, and see how much money comes to [one] beit se'ah, and then we appraise how much its value has decreased on account of this bare patch of a garden-bed. And if you should ask: Why was a beit se'ah mentioned [at all]? [Because] if one were to appraise the garden-bed from the outset relative to sixty se'ah — how much they were worth [before] and how much they are worth [now] — he would not pay anything, since the bare patch of a small garden-bed is not noticeable in sixty se'ah, whereas in a beit se'ah it is noticeable.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:8:3.hebrew: תרקב בששים תרקבין - שלשים סאין שמין ולא ששים, דא"כ מפסדת ליה לניזק, שאין קונין מצויין לששים סאין, לפי שמרובין הן לאדם בינוני, ומועטין הן למשופע בנכסים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:8:3.english: A tarkav relative to sixty tarkav - Thirty se’a are appraised, and not sixty, for if so, you cause a loss to the injured party, since buyers are not commonly found for sixty se’a, because they are too much for an average person and too little for one who has abundant property.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:8:4.hebrew: קלח בס' קלחים - מה שאכלה, בס' שיעורין כמותו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:8:4.english: A stalk relative to sixty stalks - What [the animal] ate [is appraised] relative to sixty measures like it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:9:1.english: Pays their value - As a kav or two kav are sold in the market.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 58b:9:2.english: What, is it not by itself - And [this] is difficult for all of them.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 58b:15:1.hebrew: קשבא - פי' בקונטרס: דקל. וכן משמע, דקאמר: "ותלתא תאלתא בקינא הוו קיימי", ותאלי הם דקלים, כדמוכח בהחובל (לקמן בבא קמא דף צב.): "חזא תאלי בי גופני", וקאמר: "גופני קנו דקלי". וקשה, דבפ"ק דע"ז (דף יד:) תנן: "דקל טב וחצב ונקלבא", ומפרש בגמ': חצב — קשבא. ושמא יש מיני דקלים הרבה, שאחד קרוי דקל סתם, ואחד קרוי חצב, דהיינו קשבא. ובערוך פירש דקשבא הוא דקלא פרסאה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 58b:15:1.english: Kashba - Rashi explains: [It is] a date palm. And so it is implied, as [the Gemara] says: "And three date palms [talata] were standing in a cluster," and talei are date palms, as is proven in [the chapter] HaChovel (below, Bava Kamma 92a): "[He] saw talei among vines," and [the Gemara] says: "Vines acquire date palms." And this is difficult, for in the first chapter of Avodah Zarah (14b) we learned in a Mishnah: "A good date palm, and a chatzav, and a nikalva," and the Gemara explains: Chatzav [is] kashba. And perhaps there are many species of date palms, such that one is called "date palm" unqualifiedly, and one is called chatzav, which is kashba. And the Arukh explains that kashba is a Persian date palm.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 58b:15:2.hebrew: דדאין דינא דפרסאה - י"מ של דקל פרסאי, דאמר לקמן: "הלכתא כוותיה דריש גלותא בדקלא פרסאה". ולפי מה שפירש בערוך דקשבא דקלא פרסאה, אי אפשר לפרש כן:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 58b:15:2.english: Who rules according to Persian law - Some explain [that it means the law] of a Persian date palm, as [the Gemara] states later: "The halakha follows the Exilarch regarding a Persian date palm." But according to what is explained in the Arukh, that kashba is a Persian date palm, it is impossible to explain [it] thus.
